chapters.name: INTRO
chapters.summary: A transaction groups many steps into one unit: all of them happen, or none do.

chapters.name: THE PROBLEM
chapters.summary: Two separate UPDATE statements lose ₹300 when the server crashes between them.

chapters.name: BEGIN · COMMIT · ROLLBACK
chapters.summary: BEGIN and COMMIT make both updates atomic, while a crash before COMMIT rolls everything back.

chapters.name: ACID
chapters.summary: Atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability are the four guarantees of a transaction.

chapters.name: ISOLATION ANOMALIES
chapters.summary: Dirty reads, non-repeatable reads and phantom reads show what happens when concurrent transactions see too much.

chapters.name: ISOLATION LEVELS
chapters.summary: The SQL standard defines four isolation levels that block more anomalies at the cost of concurrency.

chapters.name: DURABILITY · WAL
chapters.summary: A write-ahead log flushed before COMMIT lets the database replay committed changes after a crash.

chapters.name: IN CODE
chapters.summary: In Quarkus, @Transactional wraps a method, and checked exceptions still commit unless you opt in to rollback.

chapters.name: RECAP
chapters.summary: Group the steps and treat them as a single unit: a transaction either fully happens or never happened.
